cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Pick a Priority
cards.instruction: Make someone choose between two ordinary obligations that both supposedly cannot wait.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I approve one collection before six: your mother at the station or her parcel before the depot shuts. Choose.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can you get the parcel first? It's her birthday present.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Parcel priority is approved. You may explain to your mother why her present is being collected before she is.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll call her now. Keep driving to the depot.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: She's calling me first. Stopping to explain means missing six. I authorize either the explanation or the parcel; which do you want delivered?

heightening.evidence: B4 solution becomes A5 a new priority choice tied to the same closing deadline, not an unrelated task.
